newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Mining to lift non-ferrous output.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Mining to lift non-ferrous output.

text.p: Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co, Japan's largest zinc refiner, said on Friday it planned modest increases in its output of refined zinc, copper and lead in the half-year ending March 1997 from the same year-ago period.
Zinc output was forecast at 82,500 tonnes versus 80,200 tonnes a year earlier, copper at 79,700 tonnes versus 78,800 tonnes and lead at 34,300 tonnes versus 32,600 tonnes.
The target for zinc was also up from the April-September 1996 target of 79,000 tonnes, but copper and lead were off slightly from 80,000 tonnes and 35,000 tonnes, respectively.

The company expected year-on-year declines in gold and silver output in the upcoming October-March half-year, however, to 8,214 kilograms and 106,000 kilograms, respectively, from 8,494 kilograms and 130,700 kilograms in the same period in 1995/96.
The numbers include metal refined on a tolling basis for other companies and output from a wholly owned zinc refining subsidiary. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk (81-3 3432 6179)
